info.bio:
Salvatore Phillip "Sonny" Bono (16 February 1935 – 5 January 1998) was an American record producer, singer, actor, and politician whose career spanned over three decades.

He began his career as a songwriter, with his "Things You Do To Me" recorded by Sam Cooke and his "Needles and Pins," co-written with Jack Nitzsche, taken to hit status by The Searchers in 1964. Hired as a "gofer" by producer Phil Spector in the early 60s, Bono picked up the tools of the producing trade.

scenes.name: Discos de respuesta y country patriótico
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: «Eve of Destruction», que definió y mató la «protesta» como género efímero, provocó una avalancha de discos de respuesta: «The Dawn of Correction» de los Spokesmen, «The Revolution Kind» de Sonny Bono, «What’s Come Over This World» de Billy Carr; y el «Universal Soldier» de Donovan, «The Universal Coward» de Jan Berry. El examen más claro de la mentalidad patriótica estaba en el country, que desde mediados de los sesenta se volvió reaccionario: un baluarte frente a los cambios y frente a una cultura juvenil incomprensible, blanco, de pueblo, de clase obrera y media baja (precisamente las clases más golpeadas por la guerra), con valores cristianos y patriotismo sin preguntas; George Wallace ya lo había usado en su campaña de 1964. «The Ballad of the Green Berets» fue su apoteosis; después llegaron «Day for Decision» de Johnny Sea y «Gallant Men» del senador Everett Dirksen.

scenes.name: Los Ángeles y el Sunset Strip
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: La ciudad que en 1966 se convirtió en la meca internacional del pop. Bobby Jameson, de veinte años, en los márgenes de la industria (había grabado canciones tempranas de Jagger/Richards en Londres y se presentó al casting de los Monkees), grabó con miembros de los Leaves y el primer batería de Love «Vietnam» (Mira, octubre de 1965): órgano de película de terror, ritmo Bo Diddley y un aullido sin esperanza, el blues de un hombre blanco, retirado casi al instante. Detenido por drogas tras su primer LSD con Danny Hutton, se libró del reclutamiento al confesarlo en el examen. La adolescente Jan Smithers, habitual de Malibú y del Strip, decía a Newsweek que a veces quería gritar y golpear la almohada.

podcast.title: "She Said, Yeah" (1963) - Most Famous Song
podcast.body: His most famous song up to the point of "Needles and Pins" was "She Said, Yeah," the B-side to Larry Williams's "Bad Boy." "His most famous song up to this point was she said, yeah, the B-side to Williams's Bad Boy."

podcast.title: Alleged Abusive Misogynist Egomanic
podcast.body: Along with Jack Nitzsche and Phil Specter, Bono is described as an "abusive misogynist Ego Maniac," which is cited as a reason for Jackie DeShannon's uncredited co-authorship of "Needles and Pins." "I tend to believe her, both Nitchie and Bano were, like their boss, abusive misogynist Ego Maniacs, and it's easy to see them leaving her name off the credit."

podcast.body: As Phil Spector's assistant, Sonny Bono contributed backing vocals to The Ronettes' hit "Be My Baby," alongside his then-new girlfriend, Cher. "Notably, Spectre's assistant Sonny Bono and his new girlfriend Cher."

podcast.body: Sonny Bono was a young man who had just been hired by Bumps Blackwell as his assistant at the time of Sam Cooke's "You Send Me" recording sessions. "Things You Do To Me, which was written by a young man Bumps Blackwell had just taken on as his assistant, named Sonny Bono."

podcast.title: Control over Cher's Music
podcast.body: Sonny Bono prevented Cher from recording the song "The Night the Lights Went Out in Georgia," illustrating the control male partners/producers sometimes exerted over female artists' material choices. "When Sunny told her that she could not record the night the lights went out in Georgia and Vicki Lawrence said thank you very much."
